items.title: [tass.com] Lula wins fourth Brazilian term as Bolsonaro seeks annulment
items.content_html: Brazil’s electoral court declared President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva the winner of Sunday’s runoff, giving him a fourth, nonconsecutive term after he overcame a first-round deficit against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula received 51.79% of valid votes to Bolsonaro’s 48.21%, a margin of about 4.4 million votes. It was Brazil’s first presidential runoff in which the first-round runner-up won, according to reported results. Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, refused to concede and said he would seek to annul the result, citing a Supreme Court justice’s last-minute, two-hour voting extension. Both campaigns had requested extra voting time; authorities later said the extension applied only to polling stations that were still open. Lula now faces a legislature with stronger conservative representation. Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party holds 121 of 513 lower-house seats and 28 of 81 Senate seats, while public debt exceeds 80% of GDP. The official count is complete, and Lula is scheduled to take office on Jan. 1, 2027.

items.title: [firstpost.com] Brazil markets slide as Lula win revives fiscal concerns
items.content_html: Brazil-linked assets fell in early offshore trading Monday after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Investors had favored Bolsonaro, whom they viewed as more likely to pursue fiscal austerity and deregulation. An exchange-traded fund tracking Brazilian equities fell as much as 16% in Japan, while the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF dropped nearly 20% in overnight trading; currency derivatives signaled a possible decline of more than 10% in the real. These were early offshore moves, not Brazilian closing prices. Brazil’s electoral court gave Lula 51.79% of the vote to Bolsonaro’s 48.21%. Lula’s next term begins in January 2027. Public debt reached 82.9% of GDP in August, up more than 10 percentage points during Lula’s current term, while less than 8% of the federal budget is adjustable. Lula has pledged to protect social spending and raise the minimum wage. Investors are watching whether he can meet those pledges while stabilizing debt and inflation. Brazil’s benchmark interest rate was 13.75% and inflation was 4.6%. Inflation is not expected to reach the central bank’s 3% target until as late as 2029, Reuters reported. A consumption-tax overhaul approved in 2023 is also due to take effect in January, but the government has not disclosed its effective rate; independent analysts estimate it at about 28%.

items.title: [japantoday.com] Serbia’s student-backed list projected to win majority as Vučić concedes defeat
items.content_html: The student-backed Student List is projected to win a majority in Serbia’s parliament after former President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Sunday’s snap election, ending his Serbian Progressive Party’s 14-year dominance. Vučić said the list could take 135 to 140 of the 250 seats, against about 105 for his party; separate pollster projections put the Student List at 138 seats. The count remained preliminary. Turnout reached 67.6% by 7 p.m., the highest since Yugoslavia’s breakup in 1992. The election followed nearly two years of protests sparked by the November 2024 collapse of a railway-station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and failures of oversight, accusations the government rejected. The movement’s anti-corruption campaign drew support beyond students, and it entered the election with a slate of civil society candidates. With final results still pending, the Student List faces the task of forming a government without a single established leader. Its candidates have limited political experience. European Union officials offered help with rule-of-law and media reforms, while Vučić alleged foreign interference without providing evidence.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Brazil's Lula and Bolsonaro finish final debate with poll showing 50-50 tie
items.content_html: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their final televised debate Friday, two days before a runoff that will decide whether Lula wins a fourth nonconsecutive term or Bolsonaro succeeds him. A Datafolha poll published Thursday showed the candidates tied at 50% of valid votes, after Bolsonaro led the Oct. 4 first round with 47.03% to Lula's 45.16%. The debate on TV Globo in Rio de Janeiro was more restrained than their earlier encounter but still featured sharp exchanges over living costs, crime, government spending and corruption allegations. Lula defended wage increases and public investment; Bolsonaro said prices and household debt were rising and criticized the government's spending and tax policies. The candidates are making their final campaign push Saturday, when Brazilian election law bars broadcast campaign advertising but permits rallies. Voters are scheduled to choose between them Sunday, Oct. 25.

items.content_html:
🎨 🌾 🔭 ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Russia and Ukraine agree to Oleshky truce for aid and evacuations
items.content_html: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to pause fighting around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations under an arrangement brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, officials said Friday. Russia’s military chief and Ukraine’s General Staff said their forces would stop firing at 4 a.m. Moscow time on Oct. 27. The White House had announced Oct. 29 as the ceasefire’s start date, while Ukrainian negotiator Dmytro Lubinets, the country’s human rights ombudsman, said the humanitarian mission would begin on Oct. 29 and the pause would last several days. Oleshky’s population has fallen from about 24,000 before the invasion to an estimated 1,700-2,000, including about 50 children. Residents face shortages of food, medicine and clean water, limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks. The first steps are expected to include assessing residents’ needs and clearing mines before aid convoys enter. Civilian teams are to coordinate transport for those choosing to leave for either Russia or Ukraine. The ceasefire is expected to cover the Kherson region and neighboring areas essential to the operation. Lubinets said it would last several days; officials have not provided details on how compliance will be monitored. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said technical-level talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: [ft.com] Meta posts first free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as AI spending climbs
items.content_html:
🎨 🏔️ ✏️

Meta reported $64.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 26% from a year earlier, but recorded its first quarterly free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as it spent heavily on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. The company also disclosed a new share arrangement for Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg, who had considered leaving California over a proposed billionaire wealth tax. Meta reported $9.9 billion in net income after recording a $9.9 billion charge tied to a settlement with U.S. states over claims involving teen mental health. The company spent about $35 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter and forecast spending as much as $145 billion in 2026. The new nonvoting Class C shares are intended to help Meta raise capital for AI investment and allow Zuckerberg to sell stock without surrendering voting control. He committed to remain in California, or wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years. California voters decide the proposed wealth tax, Proposition 40, on Nov. 3, and Meta plans to issue the shares in January 2027.
